subject: Geography
central_question: How does manufacturing add value to resources, why do industries choose particular locations, and how are manufacturing systems classified?
in_scope_units: Meaning of secondary activities and manufacturing as value addition.
Classification by size: household, small-scale and large-scale manufacturing.
Classification by raw material: agro, mineral, chemical, forest and animal based industries.
Classification by output into basic and consumer goods industries.
Classification by ownership into public, private and joint sectors.
banned_topics: Detailed farming and mining systems, treated in Primary Activities.
Detailed trade, transport and communication networks, treated in later chapters.

known_pitfalls.claim: Manufacturing means only goods made by hand.
known_pitfalls.correction: Although the word literally means to make by hand, the chapter includes machine production and defines manufacturing as transforming raw materials into higher-value finished goods.

known_pitfalls.claim: An industry is located near only one factor such as raw material.
known_pitfalls.correction: Market, raw material, labour, energy, transport, communication, policy and agglomeration operate together.

known_pitfalls.claim: Footloose industries can be placed anywhere without conditions.
known_pitfalls.correction: They are less tied to specific raw materials but still depend strongly on component supply and road accessibility.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 3(ii) on trends in modern industrial activity.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1–3 and three Project/Activity tasks on manufactured goods, biodegradable materials and global brands.
